critical_code_review_comments: routes/hr.py L117-144 (_users_in_tenant): the company-based OR clause may pull users from a different parent if two distinct tenants happen to share an identical company name (rare but possible after manual edits). Consider scoping the company match by tenant_id whenever already known, or adding a unique-constraint/normalisation on user.company at signup.

routes/hr.py L289-399 (employee_timesheet): the aggregation groups by created_at[0:10] which assumes ISO-8601 strings stored in UTC. If a future writer inserts non-ISO timestamps or local times, the day bucket will be incorrect. Add a $type check or a $dateFromString conversion for robustness.

routes/hr.py timesheet uses presence_seconds = last - first of the day, which inflates 'hours_worked' when a user logs in early and the last hit is late at night (single long span). Choice 3c is documented, but consider adding a max_daily_hours cap (e.g., 12h) to prevent abuse, plus an optional break deduction config.

routes/hr.py L207-214: idempotence check filters on deleted_at=None. A soft-deleted employee with same user_id cannot be re-enrolled via POST (will succeed and create a duplicate row alongside the deleted one). Either include {'deleted_at': None or {'$exists': True}} in the conflict check and force using /restore, OR change the create endpoint to detect a soft-deleted twin and auto-restore it.

routes/hr.py: no PATCH on email_snapshot/name_snapshot — these are frozen at creation. When the underlying user updates their full_name or email, the list_employees enriches with fresh user info (good), but exports/reports built off snapshots will drift. Either drop snapshots from response or refresh them on each update_employee call.

routes/cashier.py L370-377: _is_comptable / _can_view_cashier addition is clean and minimal — 17 GET endpoint touch points all use _can_view_cashier. Recommend adding a unit-level test that enumerates all cashier router routes and asserts the dependency callable matches expectations (defence against future devs accidentally swapping _can_view_cashier back to _can_invoice).

Pydantic EmployeePayload (routes/hr.py L32-41): hourly_rate is optional even when pay_type='hourly'. The timesheet computes computed_gross = hours * (hourly_rate or 0) silently → 0. Add a model_validator to require hourly_rate > 0 when pay_type=='hourly'.
